about_meta_description: crontab.cv is an open-source visual cron expression editor built on TanStack Start, cronstrue and cron-parser.
about_meta_og_description: An open-source crontab tool with visual editing, real-time translation and multi-language code generation.
about_subtitle: An open-source tool that makes cron expressions human-friendly — visual, instant translation, shareable.
about_feat_translate_desc: Translate expressions into natural language using cronstrue.
about_feat_visual_desc: Click number grids to select multiple values; lists are merged automatically.
about_feat_code_desc: Generate Crontab, Go, Node.js, Python and Java code with a single click.
about_feat_tz_desc: Switch timezones and instantly recompute the next runs.
about_feat_share_desc: Expression and timezone are encoded in the URL — copy and share.
about_feat_theme_desc: Respects your system preference; the manual choice is remembered.
about_feedback_desc: crontab.cv is continuously improved — issues and PRs are welcome.
about_why_p1: Cron expressions look cryptic but are everywhere — Linux servers, GitHub Actions, Kubernetes, AWS EventBridge, Vercel, Cloudflare Workers. Most online tools either lack timezone support, only show a one-line translation, or can't be deeply linked.
about_why_p2: crontab.cv aims to be the fastest way to read, write and ship a cron expression: visual editing, instant translation, multi-timezone preview, shareable URLs, and ready-to-paste code for the platforms developers actually use.
about_privacy_desc: Everything runs in your browser. Expressions are never sent to a server, there is no analytics tracking your inputs, and the URL parameters never leave your device unless you explicitly share the link.
about_faq_a_privacy: No. Parsing, translation and next-run computation all happen client-side. The page is fully static and works offline after the first load.
about_faq_a_dialect: Both 5-field POSIX/Vixie cron and 6-field Quartz cron, including L / W / # / ? extensions. The Docs page has a side-by-side dialect comparison.
about_faq_a_seconds: Yes — switch to Quartz mode to enable a leading second field (6 fields total).
about_faq_a_offline: Yes. crontab.cv is a fully static SPA — once loaded, the editor and translator keep working without a network connection.
about_license_label: MIT licensed · open source on GitHub
docs_meta_description: Complete cron syntax reference: fields, special characters (* , - / ?), 20+ common examples and links to library implementations.
docs_meta_og_description: Complete cron expression syntax reference and common examples.
docs_intro_prefix: A standard cron expression is made of 5 fields separated by spaces, from left to right:
docs_examples_hint: Click any expression to apply it
docs_special_any_desc: Matches every possible value of the field. e.g. * in the minute field means "every minute".
docs_special_list_desc: Enumerate multiple values. e.g. 1,3,5 means "1, 3 and 5".
docs_special_range_desc: A continuous range. e.g. 9-17 means "9 through 17".
docs_special_unspecified_desc: Used in the day-of-month or day-of-week field to mean "not specified" (Quartz-style).
docs_ex_first_15: 1st and 15th of the month at midnight
docs_ex_first_mon: First Monday of the month at 8:00 AM
docs_nicknames_intro: Most cron daemons accept these shorthand aliases instead of a full 5-field expression.
docs_nick_monthly_desc: Once a month at midnight — equivalent to 0 0 1 * *
docs_nick_weekly_desc: Once a week, Sunday midnight — equivalent to 0 0 * * 0
docs_nick_daily_desc: Once a day at midnight — equivalent to 0 0 * * *
docs_nick_hourly_desc: Once an hour, on the hour — equivalent to 0 * * * *
docs_nick_reboot_desc: Run once at startup. Daemon-specific (Vixie cron); not portable.
docs_quartz_intro: Quartz / Spring add a few extras for fine-grained day-of-month and day-of-week selection. Available when 6-field Quartz mode is enabled.
docs_quartz_l_desc: In day-of-month: the last day of the month. In day-of-week: the last given weekday of the month (e.g. 6L = last Friday).
docs_quartz_w_desc: Nearest weekday (Mon–Fri) to the given day. e.g. 15W triggers on the weekday closest to the 15th.
docs_quartz_lw_desc: Last weekday of the month — convenient for end-of-month payroll or batch jobs.
docs_quartz_hash_desc: dow#n means the n-th given weekday of the month. e.g. 2#1 = first Monday.
docs_quartz_q_desc: Use ? in the day-of-month or day-of-week field when you specify the other — required by Quartz.
docs_dialects_intro: Cron syntax is not standardized across platforms. Pick the row that matches your runtime before copying an expression.
docs_dialect_unix_notes: Default on Linux/macOS, node-cron, robfig/cron, Kubernetes CronJob.
docs_dialect_quartz_notes: Java Quartz uses 7 fields (year optional). Spring @Scheduled uses 6 with a leading second.
docs_dialect_aws_notes: Cannot use both day-of-month and day-of-week — one must be ?. Always UTC.
docs_dialect_k8s_notes: Same as Vixie. Schedule is interpreted in the controller's timezone (often UTC).
docs_dialect_gha_notes: UTC only. Minimum interval is 5 minutes; runs may be delayed under load.
docs_pitfall_dom_dow_title: Day-of-month and day-of-week are OR, not AND
docs_pitfall_dom_dow_desc: In Vixie cron, when both day-of-month and day-of-week are restricted, the job runs whenever either matches. Use ? in Quartz to disambiguate.
docs_pitfall_tz_desc: GitHub Actions, Vercel Cron and AWS EventBridge always use UTC. The hour you write may not be the hour you expect — use the timezone selector to convert before copying.
docs_pitfall_step_desc: */20 in the minute field fires at :00, :20, :40 — not every 20 minutes from now. After :40 the next trigger is :00 of the next hour, a 20-minute gap, not a sliding window.
docs_pitfall_short_desc: Many managed schedulers (GitHub Actions, Vercel Hobby, AWS EventBridge free tier) coalesce or skip runs under high load. For sub-minute precision use a long-running worker instead.
mode_vixie_title: 5-field POSIX / Vixie cron (min hour dom month dow)
mode_quartz_title: 6-field Quartz cron (sec min hour dom month dow); supports L/W/#/?
overlap_warn: Tasks may pile up — runtime ≥ trigger interval. Consider widening the interval or shortening the task.
no_next_quartz: Quartz extensions (L/W/#/?) detected — cannot compute the next runs.
